findings.F1: The book failed on its mean daily return on days in a position (0.014 % against at least 0.05 %) and on its Calmar (0.30), because its gain is spread thin. It holds a mean absolute position of only 0.079 of the book, its summed gross gain was 176 % against 45 % of fees, and it earns 0.090 % per agitated bar on days whose range is large for the coin against only 0.014 % on small-range days.
findings.F2: In agitated bars the reversal lives almost entirely on days whose high-low range is wide against the coin's own past 60-day median range. The signed next-day excess return (long when the close is in the lower half, short when it is in the upper half) is +1.12 % (t 3.03, n 330) in w7-12 and +1.07 % (t 3.45, n 652) in w13-18 for the widest third. For the narrowest third it is -0.04 % (t -0.16) and +0.16 % (t 0.80).
findings.F3: A wide range alone is not the effect. On wide-range agitated days, whatever the close, the next-day excess return is +0.17 % (t 0.70, n 982), against +1.03 % when signed by the close's place. A wide range belongs to the idea's own theory: forced late-day flow overshoots more when the day's swing is large.
findings.F4: Grading by the close's distance from mid-range times the relative range orders the next-day excess return monotonically across its quintiles. The quintiles from highest close and widest range to lowest close and widest range give -0.55 % (t -2.12), -0.37 %, -0.15 %, +0.60 % and +0.94 % (t 3.57), about 589 cases each. Both sides pay on wide days: low-close long +1.23 % (t 3.52), high-close short +0.93 % (t 2.85).
findings.F5: By the coin's 60-day trend, the signed next-day excess return in agitated bars is strongest in falling markets: +1.17 % (n 745), with low-close long +1.33 % (t 4.50) and high-close short +1.00 % (t 3.74).
findings.F6: In rising markets the same reading gives only +0.09 % (n 769), and the book lost there, with a gross of -0.017 % per bar and -0.050 % on its shorts.
findings.F7: A falling trend alone is not the effect: in falling agitated bars the next-day excess return whatever the close is +0.20 % (t 0.99, n 738). This fits the theory that stop-outs and margin unwinds are concentrated in falling, agitated stretches.
findings.F8: The effect is spent after one day: the signed excess return on extreme closes (top or bottom fifth of the range) is +0.71 % over 1 day but +0.20 % over 2 days (n about 1360), so a longer hold would not raise the gain per day.
findings.F9: The book's deepest falls came in w11-w14 (deepest -3.4 % to -5.0 %, three of those four windows also losing or flat), while it made only +3.0 % a year.

ideas.idea: In an agitated market, the nearer a coin's daily close sits to the day's low within its high-low range, and the wider that range is against the coin's usual daily range over the past 60 days, the larger its rise over the next day.
ideas.consequence: A trader should size the low-close rebound by how wide the day's range was for the coin, betting most after wide-range days and little after narrow ones.
ideas.name: wide-range low-close rebound

ideas.idea: In a falling, agitated market, the nearer a coin's daily close sits to the day's low within its high-low range, the larger its rise over the next day.
ideas.consequence: A trader should take the close-location rebound only while the coin is in a falling, agitated stretch, and avoid it in rising markets where it loses.
ideas.name: falling-agitated low-close rebound
